summary: A Forest Service L-4 lookout on a 28-foot timber tower, built 1938 in the Okanogan NF; staffed until 1997; the lookout survived the 2021 Cub Creek 2 fire.

facts.design: 14 x 14-foot L-4 cab with catwalk on a 28-foot timber tower

access.note: Described as an active detection site still used for emergencies; no source describes public visits or overnight rental

events.note: A 1931 newspaper item, quoted on a lookout-history site, describes a house and tower built for a lookout station on First Butte; may be an earlier station
Built by the Forest Service; the register and the Methow Valley FFLA both give 1938 for the current structure
Staffed year-round as a World War II aircraft warning station; two people per station on 12-hour shifts
Ground house, originally a garage or woodshed, converted to sleeping quarters for spotters
Returned to staffing five days a week during the 1999 fire season, after emergency-only use in 1998
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, November 8, 2000
Freshly painted by volunteers from the National Forest Foundation and Filson before the fire
Cub Creek 2 fire, July 2021, severely burned much of the summit; the ground house was lost and the lookout survived

corrections.why: Both the register and firelookout.com give a 28-foot tower, about 8.5 m. The 40.0 figure is not a metre value for this tower; it matches the 40-foot height tag on the OpenStreetMap way, which is a different measure.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and the Methow Valley FFLA date the current structure to 1938. A 1931 newspaper item quoted on a lookout-history site describes a house and tower built for a lookout station on the same peak, which suggests an earlier station. The story reports both and does not settle it.
The register gives 5,417 ft (1,651 m), which matches the record's elevation_m of 1651.1. The firelookout.com page gives 5491'. Both are reported in the story and neither is treated as settled.

notes_for_editor: Access is not established. The sources describe the lookout as an active detection site used for emergencies and say nothing about public visits, so access is recorded as restricted with that note. Build date: 1938 for the current structure per two sources; a 1931 newspaper item on the Weebly site points to an earlier station, and this is reported as a conflict. Elevation: 1651 m (5,417 ft) on the register versus 5,491 ft on firelookout.com and the Methow Valley page; the Methow page's elevation line uses a prime character and was not quoted. The Methow page has the 2021 fire and paint details; the 2021 fire is recorded as a fire event. Read budget: seven page reads, one over the six-read cap. The seventh was a TrailChick grep that added no story facts. The OpenStreetMap way page and the firelookout.org Washington list were read only to check the record, not for story facts. The 1932 fire report and the 1962 weather-station note that appear in search results were not read and are not used.
